name: Christ the Redeemer, Rio de Janeiro
fact: One of the most photogrammetry-scanned landmarks on Earth, it shows up in nearly every 3D Tiles demo reel.

name: Half Dome, Yosemite
fact: Its granite face has been laser-scanned so many times it practically has its own point cloud fandom.

name: Mount Everest
fact: Its official height has been re-surveyed multiple times, most recently jointly by Nepal and China in 2020.

name: Sydney Opera House
fact: Its curved shells were originally impossible to engineer until someone realized they could all be cut from the same sphere.

name: Grand Canyon
fact: It's a favorite terrain-tile stress test since it has both massive scale and brutal elevation change.

name: Burj Khalifa, Dubai
fact: Tall enough that its upper floors see the sunset several minutes later than street level.

name: CN Tower, Toronto
fact: Held the record for world's tallest freestanding structure for over 30 years.

name: Antarctica, McMurdo Station
fact: One of the few places on Earth where satellite imagery updates are more exciting than the news.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza
fact: Its base is level to within about 2 centimeters, still baffling modern engineers.

name: Silicon Valley, California
fact: Ground zero for most of the AR/VR headsets currently gathering dust in people's closets.

name: Mount Fuji, Japan
fact: Its near-perfect symmetry makes it one of the most recognizable digital elevation models in any dataset.

name: Iceland's Þingvellir Rift
fact: You can literally stand between two tectonic plates as they slowly pull apart.
